tldr: Conditional treatment-distribution ordering can fail within covariate groups even when every marginal distribution comparison and every conditional mean comparison agrees. On the unchanged continuous-density class with one-tenth H\"older assignment and baseline and a Lipschitz density contrast, original-likelihood cone priors and finite full-null tests prove critical-radius orders \(n^{-1/4}\) for unknown assignment and \(n^{-1/3}\) for disclosed assignment, each up to logarithmic factors. The assignment-information ratio has polynomial order \(n^{1/12}\) up to logarithms and tends to infinity. The new consolidated theorem is the headline; the two logarithmic radius gaps and the exact slowly varying ratio factor remain open.
